transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because... even on my better days, I just can't shake this feeling. It's the people at my church, and the ones in my walking club. I know they're watching me, and they keep putting these little messages about me in the Sunday bulletin, or hiding things in what they say to me. 

Speaking of the bulletin, Brenda is the one who prints them, and she recently switched to this awful, flimsy paper. She claims it's because of the church budget, but her husband just bought a brand new camper. A big one, too, with the pull-out sides. My husband and I used to have a camper back in the eighties, we'd take it all the way up to the lake... the mosquitoes were just terrible up there, though. I swell up so badly when I get a mosquito bite, I have to use that pink lotion. 

But anyway, what was I... oh, yes. The messages in the bulletin. It just makes me very uncomfortable when I go to walk or to service.
Do you think the messages in the Sunday bulletin are actually about you, or is it just a feeling you have?

Oh, no, it's not just my imagination. Like I was saying, even on my better days, I just can't shake it. I know for a fact those people at church and in the walking club are watching me. I can tell they're putting those little messages in the bulletin on purpose, or slipping things into what they say to me. 

Just the other day at the walking club, Susan said something about "keeping a steady pace," and I knew exactly what she meant by that. Susan always wears those bright pink tracksuits, by the way. I don't know where she finds them. It reminds me of the tracksuits my sister used to wear. She lived down in Florida, so she wore them year-round. It gets so terribly humid down there, I really don't know how she stood it. I went to visit her once in July and my hair just frizzed right up like a poodle. I had to wear a sun hat the entire trip just to look decent. 

But, um... what was I saying? Oh, right. Yes. I know they're doing it. It's definitely not just a feeling I have, they really are putting those messages in there.
Do you often find it difficult to stay on topic when talking to someone?

Well, yes, I suppose I do. Like when I try to explain things to people... I might start with one thought, maybe about the mail, or what happened at church, and then somehow I end up talking about quilt patterns. My grandmother used to make the most beautiful quilts, you know. She had this one pattern, the Double Wedding Ring, and she used all these little scraps of calico fabric she saved from making our dresses. She never threw anything away, not even a single button. She kept them all in this big blue tin that used to have those Danish butter cookies in it. I always loved those cookies, especially the ones with the little coarse sugar crystals on top, they were just so good with a warm cup of tea in the afternoon... 

But, oh, I'm sorry, what was I saying? Right, staying on topic. Yes, I'll start with the mail and end up talking about the quilts, or the birds outside my window, or the warnings I see. And then I can just look at people's faces and see they have absolutely no idea what I'm getting at. The point just sort of slips away from me.
Do you feel like your thoughts are disjointed or hard to follow when you're talking to someone?

Well, yes, I suppose that's what I was just trying to say. When I try to explain things, I might start with one thought, like about the mail or church, and then somehow I end up talking about quilt patterns, or the birds outside my window, or those warnings. The birds have been so active lately, especially the blue jays. They are just terribly bossy at the feeder. I put out those black oil sunflower seeds because the cardinals like them, but the blue jays just swoop in and chase everyone else away. My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, he has a squirrel-proof feeder, but the squirrels figured it out anyway. They are so clever, really. He was out there yesterday waving a broom at them... 

Oh, but I'm doing it again, aren't I? Yes, I can just look at people's faces and see they have absolutely no idea what I'm getting at. The thoughts just get all jumbled up and hard to follow.
Have you always had trouble staying on topic and following your thoughts, or is this something that has developed over time?

Well, no, it hasn't always been like this. It really all started about eleven months ago. The voices, those messages in the bulletin, and just this... this trouble keeping my thoughts straight. It's been about eleven months. 

Before that, I was always very organized. I used to keep a planner, a little leather-bound one that I bought at the stationary store downtown. They closed that store a few years back, which is a shame because they had the most wonderful selection of fountain pens. I bought my niece a beautiful silver one for her high school graduation. She went on to study nursing, you know. She works at the county hospital now, mostly in the pediatric wing. She says the children are just so resilient, but I don't know how she handles seeing them sick. I could never be a nurse, the sight of blood just makes me feel terribly faint. I remember once when I was slicing tomatoes for a salad...

Oh, dear, I've lost the thread again, haven't I? But yes, to answer your question, it hasn't always been this way. Just for the last eleven months or so.
Do you ever hear voices or sounds that other people can't hear?

Well, yes, I do. Sometimes, especially when the house is very quiet, I'll hear my name being called. Or just a few words, and it sounds exactly like my friend's voice coming from the kitchen or out on the porch. My friend Martha, she used to come over all the time and we'd sit on the porch. We had these lovely white wicker chairs out there. I bought them at an estate sale over on Elm Street years ago. You have to be so careful with wicker, though, because it gets terribly brittle if you leave it in the sun too long. I used to rub lemon oil on them every spring. The smell of lemon oil always reminds me of my mother doing her spring cleaning. She was absolutely meticulous, she made us take all the heavy wool rugs out to the yard and beat them with this wire contraption... 

Oh, what was I saying? Right, the voices. Yes, I'll hear her voice so clearly from the porch or the kitchen that I actually answer out loud. I'll call back to her before I suddenly remember that nobody is even there.
Do you think your way of talking and thinking has changed significantly over the past eleven months?

Well, yes, absolutely. It's just like I was telling you a minute ago. I'll start off trying to explain something simple, like the mail or church, and before I know it, I'm rambling on about the birds or those warnings or quilt patterns. I used to quilt quite a bit, actually. I made a beautiful double wedding ring quilt for my sister's anniversary. I used this lovely blue calico fabric I found at a little shop in the next town over. The woman who ran it had the most beautiful collection of antique thimbles displayed in a glass case by the register. She said her husband brought them back from his travels in Europe. They went to France, I think... or maybe it was Italy. I've always wanted to see Italy, the food just looks so wonderful on those television programs. I love a good pasta, though tomatoes give me terrible heartburn these days... 

Oh, dear. See? There I go. But yes, it's changed so much in these last eleven months. I just drift off like that, and I look up and see people staring at me because they don't know what on earth I'm getting at anymore.
Do you think the voices you hear are coming from inside your head or from outside?

Well, they definitely sound like they're coming from outside my head. Like I was saying before, it's usually when the house is just perfectly quiet. I'll hear my name, or just a few words, and it sounds exactly like my friend Martha is standing right there in the kitchen, or maybe out on the porch. The porch really is lovely in the evenings. We used to sit out there with a glass of iced tea and watch the fireflies. Martha makes the best iced tea, she always puts a sprig of fresh mint in it. She grows it in a little terracotta pot by her back door. Mint is so invasive, though, you really have to keep it contained or it will just take over your entire garden. I tried growing tomatoes one year, but the squirrels got to almost every single one of them before they even ripened... 

Oh, excuse me. I'm doing it again. But yes, to answer you, the voice sounds so real and so much like it's coming from the other room that I'll actually answer out loud. I'll call back to the kitchen before it hits me that I'm completely alone in the house.
Do you think your thoughts are more disorganized than they used to be?

Well, yes, I suppose they are. Like I said just a moment ago, it's just so frustrating. I'll start out trying to explain something simple, you know, just an ordinary thought about the mail or maybe something from church on Sunday. Pastor Thomas gave such a lovely sermon last week about forgiveness. He has this booming voice that just fills the whole sanctuary. The sanctuary has these gorgeous stained glass windows, they were donated by the Miller family back in the fifties. Mrs. Miller used to bring the most incredible pecan pies to the church bake sales. I tried to get her recipe once, but she said it was a secret passed down from her grandmother. I love baking, but my oven has been acting up lately. It doesn't heat evenly, so my cookies always burn on the bottom...

Oh, dear, I've done it again, haven't I? But yes, my thoughts are just so scattered. I'll start with the mail or church, and before I know it, I'm going on about quilt patterns or the birds outside, or those warnings... and then I look up and I can see the person I'm talking to just looking at me, and I know they have absolutely no idea what I'm getting at.
Do you believe the messages you think you're seeing in the Sunday bulletin are actually there, or are they just something you interpret as messages?

Well, I really do believe they are actually there. Even on my better days, I just can't shake the feeling that some people at church, and even in my walking club, are watching me and putting little messages about me right there in the printed bulletin, or hiding things in what they say to me. The walking club meets on Tuesdays over at Centennial Park. It's such a lovely park, especially right now with all the little ducklings out on the pond. I brought some old bread to feed them last week, though my neighbor told me you're actually supposed to feed them frozen peas now. Can you imagine? I always keep a bag of peas in the freezer, but that's mostly for when my knees act up. Ice packs are just too stiff, you know, but a bag of peas molds right to the joint. My arthritis has been just terrible with all this rain we've been having lately. The weatherman on channel four said it's supposed to rain all the way through Thursday...

Oh, my goodness, I'm so sorry. I'm drifting off again. But yes, to answer your question, I really do feel like those messages are real and they are putting them in there on purpose.
Do you think your disorganized thinking is the main problem you're experiencing right now?

Well, I don't really know if it's the main problem. I mean, it's bothersome, certainly. But sometimes I think the sadness is worse, or just feeling so heavy all the time. It’s like carrying around a wet wool blanket. Have you ever tried to wash a wool blanket? You really have to be so careful or it will shrink right up. My mother had this beautiful Pendleton blanket, a lovely plaid pattern with deep greens and reds. She kept it folded at the foot of the guest bed. That guest room always smelled like cedar and lavender because she kept little sachets in the dresser drawers. I tried making my own lavender sachets last summer from the bushes out front, but I think I picked them too late in the season because they barely had any scent at all. The bees certainly loved them, though. We had so many bumblebees this year, the big fuzzy ones. They're much gentler than yellow jackets. A yellow jacket stung my grandson right on the ear last Fourth of July...

Oh, I'm so sorry, there I go again. But no, I wouldn't say the scattered thoughts are the absolute worst part. It's just one piece of everything that's been going wrong lately.
Do you feel sad or depressed most of the time?

Well, yes, I suppose I do feel sad most of the time. It's just this awful heaviness, like I mentioned. It settles right in my chest and makes it hard to even want to get out of bed in the morning. My bed is right by the window, and usually I love watching the sunrise. The sky gets all pink and orange, just like a peach. I used to can peaches every August with my sister, Martha. We'd buy them by the bushel from a little farm stand out on Route 9. The man who ran it, Mr. Henderson, always wore these bright red suspenders. He had a dog, a golden retriever named Buster, who would just lay under the table and thump his tail whenever anyone walked up. Buster was such a good boy. I haven't had a dog since my little terrier, Scruffy, passed away five years ago. It's just too much work now, what with the vet bills and having to walk them in the snow. The snow last winter was just dreadful, wasn't it? The plow completely blocked my driveway for three days... 

Oh, dear me, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I'm sorry. But yes, the sadness is there almost all the time. It just feels like a dark cloud that won't blow away.
Do you believe that the messages you think you're seeing are specifically about you or something that could apply to anyone?

Well, yes, I really do think they're specifically about me. That's actually why I originally came in to see someone. Even on my better days, I just can't shake the feeling that some people at church and in my walking club are watching me, and they're putting those little messages about me right in the Sunday bulletin, or hiding them in what they say when we chat. The walking club is usually so nice, though. We walk all around Centennial Park, past the big oak trees. Did you know oak trees don't even produce acorns until they're about fifty years old? I read that in a magazine at the dentist's office last month. Dr. Evans is a wonderful dentist, very gentle, but his waiting room is always freezing. I have to bring a sweater every time. I knitted this lovely yellow cardigan last winter, just a simple garter stitch, but it took me forever because my arthritis was flaring up so badly. The yarn was a wool blend, very soft, but it shed everywhere. I was finding yellow fuzz on my dark slacks for weeks...

Oh, my goodness, I'm wandering off again, aren't I? I apologize. But yes, the messages definitely feel like they are meant just for me, like they're watching what I do.
Do you think the people who are supposedly watching you and leaving messages are trying to harm you?

Well, I don't know if they want to physically hurt me, but they're definitely doing it on purpose. Like I said, I came in because even on my better days, when the sadness isn't quite as heavy, I just can't shake that feeling. I know they're watching me at church and at the walking club, and they keep putting those little messages about me in the Sunday bulletin, or hiding them in the things they say to me. The church bulletin used to be so simple, just the hymns and the prayer list. Mrs. Higgins used to type it up on an old typewriter. You could always tell when she made a mistake because she'd use that white correction fluid, and it would leave a little bumpy spot on the paper. I haven't seen a bottle of that stuff in years. Everything is done on computers now. My grandson tried to show me how to use a tablet last Christmas, but my fingers just couldn't get the hang of tapping the screen right. He's so good with technology, though. He just graduated from college with a degree in... oh, what was it called? Something with information systems. We had a lovely party for him in the backyard, with a big sheet cake from the bakery downtown. The bakery makes the best buttercream frosting, not too sweet, just perfect. They use real butter, you can taste it... 

Oh, dear, I'm so sorry, I've lost the thread again. But yes, I just know they're watching me and leaving those messages, even when I'm having a good day. It just makes me feel so uneasy.
Do you think the voices you hear and the messages you see are connected to each other?

I'm not really sure if they're connected, to be honest. The messages feel so deliberate, but the voices... well, sometimes when the house is just perfectly quiet, I'll hear my name or a few words coming from the kitchen or out on the porch. It sounds exactly like my friend's voice, and it's so clear that I actually answer back before I remember that nobody is even there. 

My friend Margaret, she always had such a carrying voice. We used to sit out on that porch for hours in the summer, just shelling peas or drinking iced tea. I always make my tea with a little sprig of mint from the garden. Mint spreads like absolute wildfire, you know. I planted one tiny little pot of it near the steps about ten years ago, and now it's completely taken over the side bed next to the rhododendrons. The rhododendrons didn't bloom very well this spring, though. I think that late frost we had in April really nipped the buds before they could open. It was so cold that week, I had to bring all my potted ferns inside to the living room, and they made such a mess on the carpet... 

Oh, goodness me, I've done it again, talking about my plants. I'm so sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, the voices and the messages. I just don't know if they have anything to do with each other. The voices just happen when I'm all alone and the house is still.
Do you think your thoughts are more disorganized than they used to be, or is it just your feelings of being watched that bother you the most?

Well, I do think my thoughts get a bit jumbled up lately, more than they used to. It's like... when I try to explain things to people, I'll start out with one thought, maybe about the mail or something that happened at church, and before I know it, I end up talking about quilt patterns, or the birds at the feeder, or those warnings I feel like I'm getting. And then I look at their faces, and I can just see they have no idea what I'm getting at. 

Speaking of quilt patterns, I used to do the most beautiful Double Wedding Ring quilts. They are so tricky because you have to piece together all those curved edges. You really need a good, sharp rotary cutter. I bought a new one at the craft store last month, the one with the ergonomic handle. The girl at the register was so young, she couldn't have been more than sixteen. She had her hair dyed this bright, shocking pink color. I don't understand why young people want to put all those chemicals in their hair. When I was her age, we just used a little lemon juice and sat in the sun if we wanted highlights. The sun was so hot that summer of '74... 

Oh, dear, I'm doing it right now, aren't I? Just wandering off. I'm sorry. But yes, the disorganized thoughts are definitely there, not just the feeling of being watched. It's very frustrating when I can't seem to make a straight point anymore.
Have you experienced any significant losses or particularly stressful events in the last eleven months?

Well, not in the last eleven months, exactly. But this has all been going on since not long after my close friend died, which was about a year and five months ago. That was... that was very hard. I mentioned Margaret earlier, didn't I? We were so close. Her funeral was on a Tuesday, and it just poured rain the entire morning. The poor pastor almost slipped in the mud right there by the graveside. 

They had a really lovely reception afterward in the church basement, though. The potato salad they served was just wonderful. I asked her sister for the recipe, and she told me the secret was using sweet pickle relish instead of dill. I've always used dill, myself. My mother taught me to make it with dill and a little sprinkle of paprika on top so it looks pretty in the bowl. Paprika doesn't really have much flavor, does it? It mostly just adds color. I actually bought a new jar of it at the grocery store last week because I noticed mine had expired way back in 2019. Can you believe they put expiration dates on dry spices now? I feel like back in the day, you just kept a little tin of it in the cupboard until it was empty. Those old metal spice tins were so charming, the ones with the little sliding lids... 

Oh, but you asked about stressful events. I suppose Margaret passing away was the biggest one, even if it was a bit more than eleven months ago. I still miss her every day.
Do you believe the messages you think you're seeing are meant for you specifically or could they apply to anyone else?

Well, I really do think they're meant just for me. That's actually why I ended up coming in to see you. Even on my better days, when I'm not feeling quite so down, I just can't shake this awful feeling that some people at church, and the ladies in my morning walking club, are watching me. And they put these little messages about me right there in the Sunday bulletin, or they slip them into the things they say when we're walking. 

We usually walk at the park on Elm Street, the one with the big duck pond. The ducks have been so aggressive lately, though. One of them actually chased Shirley all the way to the drinking fountain last Tuesday. Shirley always brings those little oyster crackers in her pocket to feed them, even though there's a big sign right by the parking lot that says "Please Do Not Feed the Waterfowl." The sign is painted this dreadful shade of forest green with yellow lettering. It reminds me of the uniform my brother wore when he worked at the hardware store back in the eighties. He hated that job. He always said the smell of fertilizer gave him a terrible headache. I can't stand strong smells either, especially lavender. People always say lavender is supposed to be relaxing, but to me, it just smells like old soap. My grandmother used to keep bars of lavender soap in all her dresser drawers to keep the moths away...

Oh, goodness, I'm wandering off again, aren't I? I'm sorry. But yes, the messages in the bulletin and the things they say... I really do feel like they're directed right at me, not anyone else.
Do you think it's possible that the messages you're seeing and the voices you're hearing might not be real?

Well, I... I suppose anything is possible, but they feel so real to me. I mean, that's really why I came in to see you in the first place. Even on my better days, you know, when I'm not feeling quite so low, I just can't shake this terrible feeling that some people at church and the ladies in my walking club are watching me. And they put those little messages about me in the Sunday bulletin, or they slip them into the conversation when we're walking. 

Like last week, the bulletin had this whole section about "tending your own garden." Now, I know they were talking about spiritual growth, but I just felt like they were pointing fingers at my actual garden. My hydrangeas haven't bloomed right in two years. I think the soil is too alkaline, but I keep forgetting to buy that acidifier stuff at the nursery. The nursery is just down the road from the new bakery that opened up. Have you been there yet? They make these wonderful lemon scones. I bought a half dozen on Tuesday, and they put them in this beautiful pink pastry box tied with baker's twine. I always save baker's twine. You never know when you might need it to tie up a roast or bundle some old newspapers. My husband used to read the newspaper every single morning. He’d sit in his armchair with his coffee—black, no sugar—and read the whole thing front to back. The ink used to get all over his fingers. He had such strong hands...

Oh, dear, I'm sorry. I'm doing it again, aren't I? Just drifting off. But to answer your question, no, I... I really feel like the messages are real. It's just so hard to explain.
Do you believe that the people who are supposedly watching you and leaving messages are capable of controlling your thoughts or actions?

Well, controlling my thoughts? Goodness, I don't think so. I haven't felt like they can get inside my head or make me do things. But like I've been saying, it's just this... this awful feeling that I can't shake. Even on my better days, you know, when the sadness isn't quite so heavy, I just know that the people at church and the ladies in my walking club are watching me. And they keep putting those little messages about me in the Sunday bulletin, or saying things when we're walking. 

We missed our walk yesterday because it was raining so hard. It rained all afternoon, just came down in buckets. My gutters couldn't even handle it. I really need to get someone out to clean them. The leaves from the big oak tree in the front yard get stuck in there every autumn. The leaves are beautiful when they turn, though. Such a lovely shade of red and gold. My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, he has a maple tree that turns the most vibrant orange. He's always out there raking. He has one of those old-fashioned bamboo rakes. You don't see those much anymore. They make such a distinct scratching sound on the concrete, don't they? It's almost musical if you listen to it long enough. He usually wears this old plaid flannel shirt when he's doing yard work. It has a little tear on the left elbow...

Oh, but no, to answer your question, they aren't controlling my actions or my thoughts. Just watching me and leaving those messages.
